heredity-environment-designs.alt: Left panel, twin study: identical twins share all their genes; fraternal twins share about half, like other siblings. Both kinds grow up in the same home at the same time. If identical twins are more alike on a trait than fraternal twins, genes contribute to differences in that trait. Right panel, adoption study: an adopted child shares genes with the biological parents and a home with the adoptive parents. Being more like the biological parents is evidence for heredity; being more like the adoptive parents is evidence for environment. A note says most traits show both.
